claims.statement: hak.selector-path v1 deterministically preserves object/array structure and provider array order, distinguishes direct presence from vacuous satisfaction for empty wildcard arrays, rejects duplicate JSON object keys/non-standard numeric constants, and requires every existing wildcard element to satisfy required descendants.

Missing required containers, wrong container types, required descendant absence, invalid or ambiguous JSON, selector type drift, or interpreter-byte mismatch cannot yield successful normalization or observation issuance.

NormalizationExecutionReceiptV1 binds exact raw bytes, content-bound HAK-013 policy, import-time interpreter source bytes/artifact refs, selector evidence state, selected payload, terminal status, and canonical digests; stronger input validation deterministically replays normalization and rejects coherent redigested forgeries.
Failed and Partial normalization attempts remain valid terminal receipts while observation issuance is permitted only for Succeeded executions.

required_checks.description: Resolve, checkout, and assert the exact PR head.
Compile HAK-013 policy and HAK-014 execution tooling under Python 3.12.
Validate HAK-014 receipt schema syntax and schema-parity tests.
Lint the HAK-014 machine-readable qualification plan.
Lint the HAK-014 HAK-010 precommitted check-binding policy against the exact HAK-014 plan.
Run focused HAK-014 execution and schema regressions.

required_negative_cases: existing wildcard element missing required descendant
coherently redigested selected result replay mismatch
empty required wildcard mislabeled as direct presence
optional selector mislabeled as vacuously satisfied

independence.claim_interpretation: limited to HAK-014 deterministic normalization execution and receipt bookkeeping; does not establish provider authenticity, semantic truth, or runtime authority
